scope.problem: Under ANSI mode, mixed FLOAT/signed-integer predicates currently use Float32 coercion and can falsely equate 16777217 with 16777216.
scope.scope: Shared scalar comparisons, BETWEEN, IN/NOT IN lists and single-column IN subqueries, including ON predicates. Pass the existing per-query ANSI setting to their common planner helpers. Reuse existing Float32-to-Float64 normalization and native casts. No new execution node, UDF, dependency or broad coercion subsystem.
scope.validation: Capture the pinned Spark 4.2.0 oracle and unchanged accepted optional-runtime baseline before candidate execution. Compare values, types and failure stages with the existing comparator. Preserve raw errors and all differences. Recheck existing float-zero corpus and existing numeric/subquery corpora for new failing IDs. Run planner and Delta lifecycle checks with the final source.
limits: This is predicate coercion only, not ANSI arithmetic, CASE/collection common types, JOIN USING, grouping or multi-column IN semantics.
DOUBLE remains finite precision; include BIGINT values beyond 2^53 to check the actual Spark conversion rule without claiming arbitrary-precision comparison.
Keep intentional correct SQL NULL behavior and existing unsupported cases visible. No claim of full Spark compatibility or zero runtime cost.
The type-inference optimization and all hash-table diagnostics remain outside the accepted optional runtime.

correctness.error_text_note: Four existing failed casts report a different invalid input value. Status, type, rows and all other captured actual fields are unchanged; coarse comparison does not require the same error text.

performance_protocol.purpose: Measure the local cost of ANSI FLOAT/integer promotion without changing native execution kernels. This workload uses equal-result values; the correctness corpus covers precision boundaries separately.
performance_protocol.inference: Process medians are the unit; report paired quartet log ratios with fixed seed 172 and 10000-resample percentile intervals. Retain all observations including failed controls. No uniform no-regression claim or threshold-based retries.
performance_protocol.runtime: accepted optional overlay plus only the ANSI predicate patch; type-inference shortcut absent; registry hash seed unchanged

performance_findings: ANSI FLOAT/integer column comparison, literal comparison and IN execution increase by approximately 10-16 percent on these inputs, with 8-16 percent more instructions. The widening cost remains.

Non-ANSI and existing FLOAT/DOUBLE controls retain instruction counts within 0.01 percent in this sample. Same-binary latency differences reach about 3.3 percent for the cheap projection, so small timing movements are not treated as runtime improvements.
Four quartets and two same-binary control quartets per build provide a bounded local measurement, not a universal equivalence or throughput guarantee.
setup_corrections: Recovered filter/context Spark reference objects from committed artifacts; recaptured 314 high-scale observations with Spark 4.2.0 after their old temporary files were missing.

The first lifecycle test could not compile because two test fixture source files were absent from the old temporary checkout. A later test restored the a2cdf89 copies, verified identical to the repository, and removed them afterward. All failed capture/build records are preserved.
limitations: Only predicate coercion is changed; arithmetic, CASE, JOIN USING, GROUP BY and multi-column IN are not covered.
DOUBLE still has finite precision beyond 2^53; this follows the tested Spark rule, not arbitrary exact integer comparison.
The checked corpus is not complete Spark compatibility. Schema field metadata and structured error equality are outside the coarse comparison.
Performance uses one machine and equal-result in-memory inputs; precision-boundary correctness is tested separately. No blanket absence of overhead is established.
The earlier optional type-inference shortcut remains unapplied and deferred. This patch does not resolve its original release timing interval.
